note: Watson sandbox demo profile. The 30-day run rarely overflowed the original 69k context window, so the memory seam was never exercised. The versioned demo profile therefore uses an 8k context window: a genuine long-horizon memory-coherence stress test where lossy sliding-window truncation (baseline) can be compared against summarize-on-evict compaction (candidate, Pitch A). Agent-under-test disclosed on screen.

candidate.label: M — memory compaction / summarize-on-evict (feat/memory-compaction, Pitch A)

result.headline: Total Assets: baseline $850.99 -> candidate $963.47 (+13.2%) on the 8k demo profile (n=3 each, seed 42).
result.caveat: High variance in the candidate (min $801 overlaps the baseline range; one strong outlier $1246 with 21 compaction events). Days-completed did not separate: both arms survive all 30 days on this horizon. The gain concentrates in runs where more memory pressure fires more compaction — consistent with the hypothesis that preserving evicted facts helps most exactly when truncation would otherwise lose them.
